messages.content: I want to settle the San Diego dates before we look at neighborhoods. Compare all four practical nonstop combinations for the three of us: Saturday or Friday evening going out, and Thursday or Friday coming back. Include the extra hotel night if we leave Friday. Do not buy anything yet.

Here are the flight totals for all three passengers. Saturday outbound with Friday return is $2,214. Saturday with Thursday return is $1,908. Friday evening outbound with Friday return is $1,836. Friday evening with Thursday return is $1,530. The Friday departure saves $378 on airfare in either return combination, while the Thursday return saves another $306.
Give me the actual times with those. A lower number does not help if we lose most of a day at either end.

The Saturday nonstop leaves Chicago at 8:10 a.m. and reaches San Diego at 10:32 a.m. The Friday nonstop leaves at 6:45 p.m. and arrives at 9:08 p.m. The Thursday return leaves San Diego at 5:20 p.m. and reaches Chicago at 11:18 p.m. The Friday return leaves at 4:55 p.m. and arrives at 10:53 p.m. All times are local.
So Friday evening out means seven hotel nights instead of six. What should I use for that extra night before we know the property?

For planning, I would carry $300 including taxes for the added Friday night. That turns the $1,836 Friday-to-Friday airfare into a provisional $2,136 flight-plus-extra-night figure. It is still $78 below the $2,214 Saturday-to-Friday airfare, although the difference could move once we price actual hotels.
And we would wake up there Saturday instead of landing late morning. That is probably worth more than $78 to us. Compare the usable time across all four, plainly.

Friday evening to Friday gives you seven nights, a full Saturday in San Diego, and the planned Friday beach time before the 4:55 p.m. flight. Friday evening to Thursday also gives you the full first Saturday, but the trip ends Thursday afternoon and drops the final beach day. Saturday to Friday preserves Friday but spends Saturday morning traveling; after landing, bags, and getting to the hotel, the first useful block likely begins around noon. Saturday to Thursday loses time at both ends: arrival around midday Saturday and departure late Thursday afternoon.
For the Thursday options, are we really getting much of Thursday, or do we have to leave the beach at lunch?

You would want to leave the beach area around 2:15 p.m. to retrieve bags and reach the airport with a reasonable cushion for the 5:20 p.m. departure. Thursday can still include breakfast and several morning hours, but it is not a relaxed full beach day. The Friday return allows a similar morning plus most of the early afternoon without cutting the trip a calendar day short.
Then eliminate both Thursday returns. The $306 savings is not enough to give up Friday. Between the remaining two, is there any financial reason not to leave Friday evening?

Only if the selected hotel's extra-night cost exceeds the $378 airfare savings by enough to change the calculation. At the $300 planning figure, Friday departure remains $78 cheaper and adds most of a usable day. A hotel night above $378 including tax would make Saturday departure cheaper on the combined comparison, but Friday would still provide more time in San Diego.

Use Friday evening through the following Friday for the hotel search. Carry the seven-night total and show me neighborhoods and actual properties next. Keep the Saturday outbound as a comparison point until we see the real room rates, but no ticket purchase or hold.

Understood. The hotel search will use seven nights, Friday through the following Friday. I’ll compare neighborhoods and actual properties using the $1,836 airfare for three, then show the complete trip figure with lodging. I’ll retain the Saturday-to-Friday flight at $2,214 as the six-night benchmark. The selected working flights are 6:45-9:08 p.m. outbound Friday and 4:55-10:53 p.m. returning Friday; nothing has been held, booked, or charged.
